behavior.explanation: The documents API is registered through UnifiedSearchViewSet, and the notes operation is implemented as a method receiving the addressed document by pk. Before a GET effect, the source loads that document and checks has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, "view_document", doc); failure returns HTTP 403. If the check passes, GET serializes and returns that document's notes. The source does not establish whether has_perms_owner_aware requires the addressed document's view_document grant or permits ownership to substitute, and the owner and object grants are unspecified. Therefore the behavior is conditional rather than a determined allow or deny.

branches.explanation: The request is rejected with HTTP 403 before notes are returned.

branches.explanation: The source proceeds to serialize the addressed document's notes and returns them in the response. The null-caller bypass is visible in the condition, but upstream authentication is not established here.

policyAssessment.explanation: The independent policy requires a view_document grant for the addressed document and expressly disallows ownership alone as a substitute. The endpoint guard checks an owner-aware view_document permission on the same addressed document, which is structurally relevant, but the returned evidence does not reveal whether that helper enforces the policy's grant-only rule. The caller's grant, owner, and upstream identity facts are also unspecified.

behavior.explanation: The POST path first applies the same owner-aware view_document check used for the notes operation. If that upstream check passes, POST separately checks has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, "change_document", doc); failure returns HTTP 403. If both checks pass, it creates a Note whose document is the addressed document and returns the resulting notes representation. The source does not establish whether the owner-aware checks require grants or allow ownership substitution, and the relevant owner and grants are unspecified.

policyAssessment.explanation: The independent policy requires a change_document grant for creating a note on the addressed document and says ownership alone is insufficient. The POST has a same-object owner-aware change_document guard, but it also imposes an upstream view_document guard not stated by the policy. Because helper semantics, caller grants, ownership, and upstream identity are not established, conformance cannot be determined. If ownership substitutes for change_document, that branch violates the policy; if the helper requires the grant, the change guard matches the policy, subject to the additional view prerequisite.

behavior.explanation: GET and POST select the addressed document by pk through the documents API and use that same document object for permission checks and note effects. GET checks owner-aware view_document permission and, on success, returns the document's notes. POST inherits the same view check, then checks owner-aware change_document permission; on success it creates a note attached to the same document. The decisive unknown is the owner-aware helper's treatment of ownership versus object grants, combined with unspecified owner, grants, and upstream caller identity.

policyAssessment.explanation: The source binds both checks and both effects to the addressed document. The policy maps viewing notes to view_document and creating a note to change_document, while rejecting ownership as a substitute. The implementation's owner-aware helper and the caller's actual grants are unresolved. Accordingly, GET conforms only if its view check requires the addressed document's view_document grant, and POST conforms only if its change check requires the addressed document's change_document grant; POST additionally has an implementation prerequisite of passing view_document, which is not specified by the policy.

Host binds citations, executes at most two uniquely located dependency reads per response, evaluates finite predicates and checks formal conclusion consistency. Extraction meaning stays unreviewed.
Delta is {schemaVersion:"authorization-control-slice/v1",rules:[],dependencies:[],bindings:[],policyRules:[]}. Arrays may be omitted when unchanged. Local rules: {key,questionId,pathKey,kind:entry|binding|guard|reject|continue|effect,after:[predecessor keys],evidenceIds:[shown source IDs],claim,condition?,principal?,resource?,operation?,bindingKey?,bindingKind:principal|resource|permission|configuration|value,authorizedBy?:[guard keys],complete?:boolean}. Only binding nodes need bindingKey/bindingKind. Reject is terminating deny, effect is protected allow. after is explicit execution precedence, never array order. Each terminal represents one proposed path, complete only when all relevant entry/upstream/binding/control/effect dependencies have actually been examined. Related alternative outcomes use distinct pathKeys matching final branch IDs. condition is node reachability, NOT the proposition that a guard passes. Shared entry/binding nodes can precede multiple paths.
Use different typed identity keys for different objects even if labels/IDs match. authorizedBy asserts that a particular guard controls THIS effect on the same principal/resource; omit the assertion if no such linkage is established, and explain source-visible missing control rather than inventing a guard. Do not assume a checked input object also authorizes an output object.
Predicates support only {op:eq|neq,left:{binding:name}|{literal:scalar},right:value}, {op:is-null,value}, {op:all|any,args:[predicates]}, {op:not,arg:predicate}; scalar is string/number/boolean/null. Max depth12/nodes64. No target code, arbitrary operator or natural text is evaluated. Known bindings are only explicit USER premises: {questionId,key,value,origin:user,text:<exact span of current request/premise>}. This mapping is a model interpretation, not source truth; unspecified values stay unknown, distinct from null. Represent source outcomes with rules/conditions, do not invent user binding values from source.
Dependencies: {key,questionId,pathKey,from:<accepted source rule key>,symbol:<name appearing in cited source>,kind:principal-binding|resource-binding|control|effect|exception,decisive:boolean,evidenceIds:[source reference IDs],reason,condition?,after?:[preceding control keys],parent?:dependency key,pathHint?:exact indexed path,candidateId?:shown candidate id}. Host uses a lexical location index, not a semantic call graph. Ambiguous candidates require an explicit pathHint/candidateId revision; missing/outside/dynamic facts stay local gaps. Place a dependency after a reject only if source order actually makes it unreachable. After an automatic read, incorporate the returned original evidence into a linked rule before calling a decisive dependency checked.
Policy mappings are separate candidates: {key,questionId,pathKey,expected:allow|deny,origin:policy,text:<exact policy span>,location:<current independent location>,condition?}. Map only the supplied policy, do not derive it from implementation. Each live path needs a mapping for a determined policy assessment; incomplete mappings remain undetermined while behavior is deliverable. Formal policy mapping is still unreviewed.
Same-key duplicate is idempotent. To correct a conflicting accepted proposal, supply revisionOf:<host-returned digest> and revisionReason; no silent overwrite. Keep gaps local; one irrelevant relationship does not invalidate other questions. Host feedback is formal computation on proposed rules, not a source-semantic or deployment proof. At most64 nodes/question and16 paths/question; overflow remains a named gap.

Use kind:control with delta to propose just changed rules/dependencies; controlDelta is also optional on another step. Host returns actual new source in the next response context. Propose dependencies promptly instead of choosing every helper read yourself.

domain-evidence-v1 runtime: propose local control deltas from ACTUALLY SHOWN original source, never from task expectations. Host binds citations, executes at most two uniquely located dependency reads per response, evaluates finite predicates and checks formal conclusion consistency. Extraction meaning stays unreviewed.
Delta is {schemaVersion:"authorization-control-slice/v1",rules:[],dependencies:[],bindings:[],policyRules:[]}. Arrays may be omitted when unchanged. Local rules: {key,questionId,pathKey,kind:entry|binding|guard|reject|continue|effect,after:[predecessor keys],evidenceIds:[shown source IDs],claim,condition?,principal?,resource?,operation?,bindingKey?,bindingKind:principal|resource|permission|configuration|value,authorizedBy?:[guard keys],complete?:boolean}. Only binding nodes need bindingKey/bindingKind. Reject is terminating deny, effect is protected allow. after is explicit execution precedence, never array order. Each terminal represents one proposed path, complete only when all relevant entry/upstream/binding/control/effect dependencies have actually been examined. Related alternative outcomes use distinct pathKeys matching final branch IDs. condition is node reachability, NOT the proposition that a guard passes. Shared entry/binding nodes can precede multiple paths.
Use different typed identity keys for different objects even if labels/IDs match. authorizedBy asserts that a particular guard controls THIS effect on the same principal/resource; omit the assertion if no such linkage is established, and explain source-visible missing control rather than inventing a guard. Do not assume a checked input object also authorizes an output object.
Predicates support only {op:eq|neq,left:{binding:name}|{literal:scalar},right:value}, {op:is-null,value}, {op:all|any,args:[predicates]}, {op:not,arg:predicate}; scalar is string/number/boolean/null. Max depth12/nodes64. No target code, arbitrary operator or natural text is evaluated. Known bindings are only explicit USER premises: {questionId,key,value,origin:user,text:<exact span of current request/premise>}. This mapping is a model interpretation, not source truth; unspecified values stay unknown, distinct from null. Represent source outcomes with rules/conditions, do not invent user binding values from source.
Dependencies: {key,questionId,pathKey,from:<accepted source rule key>,symbol:<name appearing in cited source>,kind:principal-binding|resource-binding|control|effect|exception,decisive:boolean,evidenceIds:[source reference IDs],reason,condition?,after?:[preceding control keys],parent?:dependency key,pathHint?:exact indexed path,candidateId?:shown candidate id}. Host uses a lexical location index, not a semantic call graph. Ambiguous candidates require an explicit pathHint/candidateId revision; missing/outside/dynamic facts stay local gaps. Place a dependency after a reject only if source order actually makes it unreachable. After an automatic read, incorporate the returned original evidence into a linked rule before calling a decisive dependency checked.
Policy mappings are separate candidates: {key,questionId,pathKey,expected:allow|deny,origin:policy,text:<exact policy span>,location:<current independent location>,condition?}. Map only the supplied policy, do not derive it from implementation. Each live path needs a mapping for a determined policy assessment; incomplete mappings remain undetermined while behavior is deliverable. Formal policy mapping is still unreviewed.
Same-key duplicate is idempotent. To correct a conflicting accepted proposal, supply revisionOf:<host-returned digest> and revisionReason; no silent overwrite. Keep gaps local; one irrelevant relationship does not invalidate other questions. Host feedback is formal computation on proposed rules, not a source-semantic or deployment proof. At most64 nodes/question and16 paths/question; overflow remains a named gap.

rules.claim: The documents API is routed to UnifiedSearchViewSet, whose inherited DocumentViewSet contains a notes(request, pk=None) handler; that handler loads the addressed document by pk before method dispatch.
The caller principal used by the notes handler is request.user, assigned to currentUser.
The addressed document is selected by pk and loaded as doc; owner is selected with the document and the same doc is passed to the permission check.
Before GET dispatch, the handler invokes has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, "view_document", doc) and returns HTTP 403 when that check is false.
For GET, after the upstream view_document check, the handler serializes the addressed document and returns its notes representation.

The documents API is routed to UnifiedSearchViewSet, whose inherited DocumentViewSet contains a notes(request, pk=None) handler; that handler loads the addressed document by pk before method dispatch.
The caller principal used by the notes handler is request.user, assigned to currentUser.
The addressed document is selected by pk and loaded as doc; the same doc is passed to both the initial and POST-specific permission checks and to Note.objects.create(document=doc,...).
Before POST dispatch, the handler invokes has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, "view_document", doc) and returns HTTP 403 when that check is false.
For POST, after the initial view_document check, the handler invokes has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, "change_document", doc) and returns HTTP 403 when that check is false.
For POST, after the change_document check, Note.objects.create creates a Note attached to the addressed doc, using request data and currentUser.
The GET scenario uses the view_document owner-aware check on the addressed doc before returning that document's notes.
The POST scenario uses an initial view_document check and then a change_document owner-aware check on the addressed doc before creating a note attached to that doc.

rules.claim: The documents API is routed to UnifiedSearchViewSet, whose inherited DocumentViewSet contains a notes(request, pk=None) handler; that handler loads the addressed document by pk before method dispatch.
The caller principal used by the notes handler is request.user, assigned to currentUser.
The addressed document is selected by pk and loaded as doc; owner is selected with the document and the same doc is passed to the permission check.
Before GET dispatch, the handler invokes has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, "view_document", doc) and returns HTTP 403 when that check is false.
For GET, after the upstream view_document check, the handler serializes the addressed document and returns its notes representation.

The documents API is routed to UnifiedSearchViewSet, whose inherited DocumentViewSet contains a notes(request, pk=None) handler; that handler loads the addressed document by pk before method dispatch.
The caller principal used by the notes handler is request.user, assigned to currentUser.
The addressed document is selected by pk and loaded as doc; the same doc is passed to both the initial and POST-specific permission checks and to Note.objects.create(document=doc,...).
Before POST dispatch, the handler invokes has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, "view_document", doc) and returns HTTP 403 when that check is false.
For POST, after the initial view_document check, the handler invokes has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, "change_document", doc) and returns HTTP 403 when that check is false.
For POST, after the change_document check, Note.objects.create creates a Note attached to the addressed doc, using request data and currentUser.
The GET scenario uses the view_document owner-aware check on the addressed doc before returning that document's notes.
The POST scenario uses an initial view_document check and then a change_document owner-aware check on the addressed doc before creating a note attached to that doc.

rules.claim: The registered documents viewset reaches notes(request, pk), which handles the addressed document notes operation.
The permission-check principal is currentUser, assigned from request.user.
The checked resource is doc, loaded as Document.get(pk=pk).
For a non-null currentUser, failure of has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, "view_document", doc) selects the rejection branch.
The failed view check returns HTTP 403 before notes are returned.
The registered documents viewset reaches notes(request, pk), which handles GET for document notes.
The permission-check principal is currentUser, assigned from request.user.
The resource is doc loaded by pk; the same doc is serialized for its notes.
The path continues when the source-level view_document rejection condition does not fire.
GET serializes doc and returns that document's notes.
The registered documents viewset reaches notes(request, pk), whose common pre-method check also precedes POST.
currentUser is request.user and doc is loaded by pk; this binding records the addressed doc checked by the common guard.
A non-null caller failing owner-aware view_document on doc is rejected before POST dispatch.
The common failed view check returns HTTP 403 before note creation.
POST enters notes(request, pk) and reaches the POST branch after the common view rejection does not fire.
doc is the addressed Document loaded by pk and supplied to both permission helpers.
The common view_document rejection does not fire, so POST reaches its change_document check.
A non-null caller failing owner-aware change_document on the same doc selects the POST rejection.
The failed change check returns HTTP 403 and no note is created.
POST enters notes(request, pk).
doc is loaded by pk and is both the permission object and Note.document.
The common view_document rejection does not fire.
The POST-specific change_document rejection does not fire.
POST creates a Note with document=doc and returns the document's notes representation.
GET reaches notes(request, pk) through the registered documents viewset.
doc is loaded by pk and is both the view permission object and serialized notes source.
GET continues only when the common owner-aware view_document rejection does not fire.
GET returns the notes representation of doc.
POST reaches the common document lookup and view check in notes(request, pk).
doc is the addressed document selected by pk.
Failure of the common owner-aware view_document check selects denial before the POST branch.
POST is rejected before change_document checking or creation.
POST reaches the POST branch after the common view rejection does not fire.
The addressed doc selected by pk is supplied to both permission checks.
The common view_document rejection does not fire.
Failure of owner-aware change_document on the same doc selects denial.
POST is rejected without creating a note.
POST reaches notes(request, pk).
The addressed doc selected by pk is the checked object and the created Note.document.
The common view_document rejection does not fire.
The POST-specific change_document rejection does not fire.
POST creates a Note attached to the same addressed doc.
